questions.stem: Which of the following is a method of producing magnetic fields?
questions.solution: Using a current-carrying conductor is a method of producing magnetic fields because electric current generates a magnetic field around the conductor. Permanent magnets already have a magnetic field and do not produce one, non-conductors do not carry current and thus do not generate magnetic fields, and batteries provide electrical energy but do not directly produce magnetic fields.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a safety measure used in electric circuits to prevent electric shocks?
choices: Using a copper wire for all connections
Connecting the live wire directly to the appliance
Connecting the metallic body of the appliance to the earth wire
Using a fuse with a lower current rating than the circuit
questions.solution: The correct answer is connecting the metallic body of the appliance to the earth wire. This ensures that any leakage of current to the metallic body keeps its potential to that of the earth, preventing electric shocks. The other options are incorrect because copper wire is standard, connecting live wire directly is unsafe, and using a higher-rated fuse can cause damage.

questions.stem: A current-carrying rod AB experiences a force perpendicular to its length and the magnetic field. What is the reason for this?
choices: The rod is not aligned with the magnetic field
The magnetic field is strongest at the ends of the rod
The rod is placed in a uniform magnetic field
The direction of force depends on the direction of current and magnetic field
questions.solution: The force on a current-carrying rod depends on the directions of both the current and the magnetic field, which is why it acts perpendicularly to both. The rod being misaligned with the field does not explain the perpendicular force. The strength of the magnetic field at the ends of the rod is irrelevant to the direction of the force. Being in a uniform field also does not determine the direction of the force.

questions.stem: In a domestic circuit, two separate circuits are used: one with a 15 A current rating and the other with a 5 A current rating. What is the main reason for this arrangement?
choices: To reduce the cost of the wiring
To ensure equal distribution of voltage to all appliances
To prevent overloading of the circuit
To increase the resistance of the circuit
questions.solution: The main reason for using two separate circuits with different current ratings is to prevent overloading of the circuit. High-power appliances are connected to the 15 A circuit, while low-power appliances are connected to the 5 A circuit. This helps avoid excessive current flow that could damage the wiring or appliances. The other options are incorrect because they do not address the primary purpose of separating circuits.

questions.stem: What is the direction of the magnetic field produced around a straight conductor carrying current?
questions.solution: The magnetic field around a straight conductor carrying current forms concentric circles around the conductor. questions.stem: An electric oven with a power rating of 2 kW is operated in a domestic electric circuit (220 V) that has a current rating of 5 A. What will happen in this situation?
choices: The oven will not receive enough voltage
questions.solution: The oven will draw more current than the circuit can handle. Using the formula P = V × I, the current required is 2000 W / 220 V ≈ 9.09 A, which exceeds the 5 A rating of the circuit. This will cause overloading, and the fuse will blow to protect the circuit. The other options are incorrect because they do not account for the current requirements of the oven.

The strength of the magnetic field
The direction of the magnetic field

hi.stem: दाहिने हाथ के अंगूठे के नियम में क्या निर्धारित करने में सहायता मिलती है?
hi.solution: दाहिने हाथ के अंगूठे के नियम में धारावाही चालक के चारों ओर चुंबकीय क्षेत्र की दिशा निर्धारित करने में सहायता मिलती है। यदि अंगूठा धारा की दिशा में होता है तो उंगलियां चुंबकीय क्षेत्र की दिशा में घूमती हैं। अन्य विकल्प गलत हैं क्योंकि नियम धारा की दिशा, क्षेत्र की तीव्रता या प्रतिरोध को निर्धारित नहीं करता है।
hi.imageAlt: एक चित्र जिसमें एक छड़ चुंबक के उत्तर और दक्षिण ध्रुव होते हैं, और चुंबकीय क्षेत्र की दिशा को दर्शाने वाली तीर होती है, जो दाहिने हाथ के अंगूठे के नियम को स्पष्ट करता है।

questions.stem: Why do magnetic field lines not intersect each other?
choices: Because a compass needle would get attracted to both poles
Because a compass needle would point in two directions
questions.solution: Magnetic field lines do not intersect each other because a compass needle would point in two directions at the point of intersection, which is not possible. This is a fundamental property of magnetic field lines, which are closed curves. The other options are incorrect because the strength of the field lines is not the reason for them not intersecting, they are not always parallel, and being closed curves is a characteristic but not the reason for them not intersecting.

hi.stem: चुंबकीय क्षेत्र रेखाएं एक दूसरे को क्यों प्रतिच्छेद नहीं करती हैं?
choices: क्योंकि एक सुई दोनों ध्रुवों की ओर आकर्षित हो जाएगी
क्योंकि वे हमेशा समांतर होती हैं
क्योंकि एक सुई दो दिशाओं में इंगित करेगी
क्योंकि वे बंद वक्र होती हैं
hi.solution: चुंबकीय क्षेत्र रेखाएं एक दूसरे को प्रतिच्छेद नहीं करती हैं क्योंकि एक सुई प्रतिच्छेद बिंदु पर दो दिशाओं में इंगित करेगी, जो संभव नहीं है। यह चुंबकीय क्षेत्र रेखाओं का एक मूल गुण है, जो बंद वक्र होती हैं। अन्य विकल्प गलत हैं क्योंकि क्षेत्र की तीव्रता उनके प्रतिच्छेद न करने का कारण नहीं है, वे हमेशा समांतर नहीं होती हैं और बंद वक्र होना एक विशेषता है लेकिन उनके प्रतिच्छेद न करने का कारण नहीं है।

choices: कारण एक चुंबकीय सुई दोन्ही ध्रुवांकडे आकर्षित होईल

questions.stem: Two identical straight wires carry the same current but are placed at different distances from a compass. What happens to the deflection of the compass needle in each case?
choices: It is the same in both cases
It is greater in the first case
It is greater in the second case
It depends on the wire's material
questions.solution: The deflection of the compass needle is greater when the wire is closer to the compass. This is because the magnetic field strength decreases with distance from the wire. questions.stem: What is the primary purpose of the earth wire in a domestic electrical circuit?
choices: To carry the main current to the appliances
To provide a path for the current to return to the source
To prevent electric shocks by keeping the metallic body at earth potential
To increase the voltage of the circuit
questions.solution: The earth wire is connected to the metallic body of appliances and ensures that any leakage of current keeps the body at the same potential as the earth, preventing electric shocks. The other options are incorrect because they describe functions of the live or neutral wires, not the earth wire.

hi.stem: घरेलू विद्युत परिपथ में पृथ्वी तार का मुख्य उद्देश्य क्या है?
choices: उपकरणों तक मुख्य धारा ले जाना
